voiceLines.text: Hi. I'm really glad you're here. This first walk is five minutes, and we'll do it sitting down.
Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat, hands resting on your thighs.
Your phone can stay in your pocket. If anything hurts, just stop. There's no wrong way to do this.
Let's begin with heel taps. Lift your heels, then set them down.
If that feels fine, lift your whole foot a little. One side, then the other. That's marching.
Let your arms swing gently, like you're walking out to the mailbox.
Nice and easy. Breathe in through your nose… and out through your mouth.
Sit tall, like a string is lifting the top of your head.
If you'd like a little more, lift your knees a bit higher. Only if it feels good.
You're doing it. This is your time.
Keep that steady rhythm. You should be able to talk, or even hum along.
In a few seconds, we'll pick up the pace, just a little.
A little quicker now. Same small steps, just a bit faster.
Still able to talk? Good. That's the right pace for you.
Ten more seconds.
And slow it down. Easy marching, nice and relaxed.
Shake out your hands if you like. Keep your feet moving gently.
One more quicker round coming up. Just thirty seconds.
Quicker again. If heel taps feel better right now, that's perfect.
Want a little more? Let your arms swing a bit bigger.
Almost there. Ten seconds.
And ease off. Slow, comfortable steps.
Notice how your legs feel right now. Maybe a little warmer.
Let's start to wind down.
Slow your feet until they rest flat on the floor.
Roll your shoulders back, slowly. Two or three times.
Take a deep breath in… and let it go.
One more breath in… and out.

Welcome back. Let's get your feet moving.
Good to see you. This walk is all at your pace.
Ready when you are. Let's start slow and easy.
Here we go. Easy steps first, and we'll build from there.
Sit toward the front of your chair, feet flat, back tall.

Use a sturdy chair with no wheels. Sit tall, away from the back.
A higher chair works best for you, with arms if you have one.
Stand near your chair so you can hold it if you need to. Feet about hip-width apart.
Stand tall with your chair close by. Soft knees, relaxed shoulders.
Clear a little space around you. Keep your chair on your left, within reach.
Shoes with good grip are best. Please skip socks on a smooth floor.
Hold on, and step onto the belt while it moves slowly.
Start your pad nice and slow. You can change the speed anytime.

Easy steps to start. Let your arms swing naturally.
Keep it light. Heels, then toes, nice and steady.

Just warming up. No rush at all.
Look ahead, not down at your feet.
Stand tall, like a string is lifting the top of your head.
Breathe easy. Your breath should stay calm here.

Ten seconds, then a little quicker.

Now let's do it together, right side first.

Together now. Nice and easy to start.
March. Our basic walking step.
The right knee lifts, the foot sets down, then the left.
Sit tall. Lift each foot a little off the floor, and set it down flat.
Stand tall. Each foot lands softly, heel first, then the toes.
For an easier version, just lift your heels. Toes stay on the floor.
For a little more, lift your knees higher, but keep them below your hips.
Keep your knees well below your hips the whole time.
Ten more seconds. Next up: March.
Heel dig. Heel out in front, toes up.
The right heel reaches forward, toes point up, then it comes back.
Slide your foot forward, rest the heel down, and pull your toes toward you.
